newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong to step up corruption watch after 1997.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong to step up corruption watch after 1997.

text.p: Graft busters will step up their vigil on corruption in Hong Kong after the British colony reverts to Chinese rule next year, the head of the territory's anti-corruption police said on Thursday.
Michael Leung, chief of the Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC), told a regional seminar on graft that criminals would be out to exploit loopholes in the transition to Chinese rule.

"Criminals are quick to exploit divergent laws, different languages and bureaucracy in separate jurisdictions. They are aware that corruption is a useful means to cover their tracks and to obtain bigger profits," Leung said.
"Although, we are just seven months away from Hong Kong's change of sovereignty, the need for strong regional cooperation will only increase, not decrease."

Leung said the ICAC and Chinese authorities had been stepping up collaboration before the change of sovereignty at midnight next June 30, when Hong Kong becomes a Special Administrative Region of China.
Leung said that Hong Kong and China's anti-corruption watchdogs would remain separate after 1997 but would cooperate closely.
Corruption has been rife in communist-ruled China in recent years, arousing fears among many people in Hong Kong that graft will spread in the territory after the handover.
